title: Signed line reductions and restriction to the derived-complete integral category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)_X$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], for any $K\in D(R)$ its derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^LR_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and the quotient-tower completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $L$ be a locally free rank-one $R$-module sheaf. Suppose every $L_n=L\otimes_R R_n$ is locally constant with finite stalks, meaning that on a pro-etale covering it is the constant sheaf associated to a finite $\mathcal O_E/\pi^n$-module. Set $L^{[0]}=R$, $L^{[m]}=L^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, and $L^{[m]}=\mathcal Hom_R(L^{[-m]},R)$ for $m<0$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]; use the same signed powers for $L_n$.

For every integer $m$ there are natural isomorphisms, compatible with quotient transitions,
$$L^{[m]}\otimes_R R_n\cong L_n^{[m]},\qquad
 (K\otimes_R^LL^{[m]})_n\cong K_n\otimes_{R_n}^LL_n^{[m]}.$$
The positive comparisons rebracket tensors, and the negative comparisons are the base-change maps on duals $\varphi\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto\overline{\varphi(x)}ab)$; these comparisons preserve evaluation.

For derived-complete $K$ [def-weil-derived-complete], the natural comparison from $K\otimes_R^LL^{[m]}$ to the specified quotient-tower completed tensor is an isomorphism, and the tensor remains derived complete. If $K$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], then both this tensor and its completed model belong to that category. Every interval $[a,b]$ containing the cohomological support [def-weil-cohomological-support] of all $K_n$ also contains the support of all the twisted reductions, and their cohomology sheaves satisfy the finite-torsion constructibility condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. The ordinary opposite-line evaluation isomorphisms restrict to this full integral category and, through the specified completion comparisons, give inverse equivalences for its completed tensor functors.

Proof (3), last sentence interpreted in the derived-complete integral coefficient convention; extracted generic reduction/restriction argument

proof.text: Fix $m$ and put $P=L^{[m]}$. On a covering with basis $e$ of $L$, tensor restriction [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] and the definition of sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] give the bases $e^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, $1$ for $m=0$, and the functional sending $e^{\otimes(-m)}$ to $1$ for $m<0$. Thus $P$ is a line. Write $Q=L^{[-m]}$. The evaluation $P\otimes_R Q\to R$ in these bases is $ap\otimes bq\mapsto ab$; its inverse sends $a$ to $ap\otimes q$. These are independent of the basis: replacing $e$ by $ue$ multiplies $p$ by $u^m$ and $q$ by $u^{-m}$. They glue to opposite-line evaluations. For $m<0$ this also explicitly gives the bidual identification with the positive power. The two triangle composites send $p$ to $p\otimes q\otimes p$ to $p$, and similarly for $q$, using the tensor constraints [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), and local basis calculation for signed powers and evaluation

proof.text: Ordinary scalar extension of a positive tensor power is the iterated balancing map $(x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_r)\otimes a\mapsto(x_1\otimes1)\otimes\cdots\otimes(x_r\otimes a)$; its inverse multiplies the scalar factors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. In degree zero use $R\otimes_RR_n=R_n$. For a negative power use the sheaf-Hom map [def-pur-sheaf-hom] $\varphi\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto\overline{\varphi(x)}ab)$. In each basis of Step 1 this is the identity $R_n\to R_n$, hence an isomorphism; its local inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same map. These formulas prove $P\otimes_RR_n\cong L_n^{[m]}=:P_n$. Applying $R_{n+1}\to R_n$ before or after any formula gives the same reduced scalar product. Evaluating the displayed functional also gives exactly the reduction of the integral evaluation, so all comparisons preserve evaluation.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); explicit dual base-change and evaluation calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor] to $P$ over $R$ and to the rank-one $P_n$ over $R_n$. These degree-zero lines are K-flat, ordinary tensor computes their unbounded derived tensor, and their cohomology functors are ordinary tensor on cohomology sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with ring map $R\to R_n$. It gives $(K\otimes_R^LP)_n\cong K_n\otimes_{R_n}^L(P\otimes_RR_n)$, hence the second comparison by Step 2. On a K-flat representative $U$ with flat terms its degree-$j$ map is the balancing identification $(U^j\otimes_RP)\otimes_RR_n\cong(U^j\otimes_RR_n)\otimes_{R_n}P_n$. Its inverse multiplies the two quotient scalars. Consequently these comparisons are compatible with the strict quotient transitions as well as natural in $K$.

Let $T$ be ordinary sheaf tensor on the right by $P$. The evaluation and coevaluation of Step 1 are an exact pairing in the symmetric monoidal module category [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Apply [lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions], with the order of the two lines chosen so that $T$ is the right adjoint. Thus $T$ preserves products, with comparison specified by $T(\operatorname{pr}_n)$. It is exact by [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor]. Countable products of these sheaves are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], and their derived-category products are termwise products [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence](2). The same product comparison therefore identifies $T(\prod C_n)$ with $\prod T(C_n)$ for arbitrary complexes, and represents the product comparison for the derived tensor functor. No claim that localization to a covering preserves products is used.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12; product preservation obtained from the exact line pairing

proof.text: Suppose $K$ is derived complete. Take its Roos triangle with the specified first map $c=(c_n)$ [def-weil-derived-complete]. Apply $T$ on the derived category: this is triangulated by [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor]. By Step 4 the two product terms become the products of $T(K_n)$, and their transition endomorphism becomes $1-s$ for that image tower, since its $n$th projection is $T(\operatorname{pr}_n)-T(t_n)T(\operatorname{pr}_{n+1})$. The balancing maps of Step 3 identify this tower with the reduction tower of $T(K)$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. They identify $T(c_n)$ with its reduction unit: on a representative $x\otimes p$ the map is $(x\otimes1)\otimes(p\otimes1)$. Thus the transported distinguished triangle has precisely the required first map, proving derived completeness of $K\otimes_R^LP$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12 and Definition 3.5.2; explicit transport of the reduction-unit Roos triangle

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $U$ of $K$ with flat terms as in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The identity resolution of $P[0]$ is admissible by [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor]. The well-definedness comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined](2) therefore identifies the prescribed completed tensor with $H(B_\bullet)$, where $H(C_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, $U_n=U\otimes_RR_n$, and $B_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(U_n\otimes_{R_n}P_n)$. There is a strict balancing isomorphism $T(\operatorname{Res}_nU_n)\cong B_n$: $(x\otimes a)\otimes p\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(p\otimes1)$, with inverse $(x\otimes a)\otimes(p\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes ab)\otimes p$. It commutes with every transition and sends the quotient of $x\otimes p$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes(p\otimes1)$. In the coordinates $H(C)^j=(\prod C_n)^j\oplus(\prod C_n)^{j-1}$ of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus], apply the product comparison of Step 4 to each summand. This gives a natural chain isomorphism $T(H(\operatorname{Res}_nU_n))\cong H(B_\bullet)$: it commutes with $d(v,u)=(dv,-du-(1-s)v)$ because the balancing maps commute with the transitions and differentials.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2; specified quotient-tower cone calculation

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] with its two fields both equal to $E$ and the same uniformizer. For derived-complete $K$ its statement gives a natural isomorphism $\eta_K:K\to H(\operatorname{Res}_nU_n)$, represented by $x\mapsto((x\otimes1)_n,0)$. Apply the exact functor $T$, then the chain isomorphism of Step 6. The resulting map $U\otimes_RP\to H(B_\bullet)$ is $x\otimes p\mapsto(((x\otimes1)\otimes(p\otimes1))_n,0)$, the quotient-tower completion comparison for this tensor, with zero shifted-product component [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. It is an isomorphism because $T(\eta_K)$ and Step 6 are. The resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] identify this very map with the specified completed-tensor model, naturally in $K$. This proves the asserted comparison, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism between derived limits.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2; identity-field completion comparison and zero-second-coordinate augmentation

proof.text: For every $n$ and $i$, Step 3 and [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor] over $R_n$ give $\mathcal H^i((K\otimes_R^LP)_n)\cong\mathcal H^i(K_n)\otimes_{R_n}P_n$. If $i\notin[a,b]$, the right hand side is zero whenever $\mathcal H^i(K_n)=0$. Thus any common interval $[a,b]$ remains a common interval, with exactly the same endpoints, in the meaning of [def-weil-cohomological-support]. This argument uses cohomological support, not Tor amplitude or a boundedness assumption on the original unbounded representative.

source.place: Proof (3), final derived-tensor sentence: preservation of the uniform cohomological bounds

proof.text: Assume $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Fix $n,i$ and a finite constructible locally closed partition on which $\mathcal H^i(K_n)$ is locally constant with finite values [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Pullback to each stratum is exact for the finite constant ring [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], and commutes with derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For degree-zero sheaves with the line factor flat this is ordinary tensor. The hypothesis on $L_n$, and Step 2 for its signed powers, make $P_n$ locally constant with finite rank-one values. On the common refinement of their trivializing covers, the tensor of the two constant sheaves has value $M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E/\pi^n}(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)\cong M$: the maps are $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus the cohomology sheaf of Step 8 is locally constant with finite values on the same partition. It is constructible. Steps 5 and 8 now give all conditions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. The completed model satisfies them as well by the isomorphism of Step 7.

source.place: Proof (3), final derived-tensor sentence: finite reduction constructibility and restriction to the integral full subcategory

proof.text: Apply the preceding steps also to $-m$. The ordinary evaluations of Step 1 induce the inverse equivalences on $D(R)$ supplied by [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor]. Both functors preserve the integral category by Step 9. Because this category is full [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], their evaluations, inverses and triangle identities restrict to it. Write $\chi_m:T_m\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat T_m$ for Step 7. The completed evaluation is the composite $\widehat T_{-m}\widehat T_m\xrightarrow{\chi_{-m}^{-1}}T_{-m}\widehat T_m\xrightarrow{T_{-m}(\chi_m^{-1})}T_{-m}T_m\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}1$, and similarly in the other order. Naturality of the $\chi$ cancels adjacent comparison maps in the two triangle composites, leaving the ordinary triangle identities. Step 2 identifies their reductions with the specified finite evaluations. Hence these comparisons and ordinary opposite-line evaluations give inverse equivalences for the completed tensor functors, as asserted.

source.place: Proof (3), final sentence: opposite twists are inverse, restricted through the completion comparisons

No SGA is cited, proof_deps equal the union of the step uses, and a reachability search finds no cycle. Mathematics: Steps 1-2 are elementary basis computations for the signed powers, the dual base-change map φ⊗a↦(x⊗b↦φ̄(x)ab) and evaluation, and they glue under basis change u^{±m}. Step 3 applies the ringed-topoi tensor-pullback node with u=id and R→R_n, and the comparison is compatible with transitions. Step 4: in lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions, U_Q⊣U_P, so −⊗P preserves products, and derived products are termwise (derived-limit-existence (2)). Step 5 carries the Roos triangle over with exactly the reduction-unit first map c, so no cone-uniqueness argument is needed. Steps 6-7 use the identity-field case of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison (it explicitly allows L=E and any scheme) to show that the specified zero-shifted-product augmentation into the completed tensor is an isomorphism. Step 8 keeps the same interval of cohomological support, not a Tor bound. Step 9 gets finite constructibility on the same strata from exact constant-coefficient pullback (A_n finite). Step 10 restricts the inverse equivalences through the full subcategory and conjugates by χ. Edge cases checked: m=0,±1, negative m, n=1, X=∅, K=0, unbounded K. Sources: the blueprint's sk-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free proof (3), last sentence, and Bhatt–Scholze 3.4.10/3.4.12/3.5.1/3.5.2, pp. 22-24. All nine tool_uses are generic black boxes and I accept them. Minor, not faults: the Step 5 balancing map is written out only in Step 6, and the hypothesis that L_n is locally constant is redundant.
